newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche's Breuer attacks EMU delay talk.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche's Breuer attacks EMU delay talk.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG chairman Rolf Breuer on Tuesday dismissed speculation that Europe's currency union project might have to be delayed and criticised the spat in Germany over fulfilling EMU deficit goals.
"There is no discussion of a delay," he told reporters at the Global 24 European Monetary Union conference.
"There is a consensus that it will remain on schedule."
Breuer, a well-established champion of the euro, also criticised the current wrangling in Germany over whether the country would hit the Maastricht Treaty budget deficit goal on the nail this year.

"It is wrong to place at the forefront mathematical places after the decimal point," Breuer said, referring to disputes about whether Maastricht called on countries to cut their budget deficits to precisely 3.0 percent of gross domestic product, or whether a slightly higher level was acceptable.
Breuer said the decision as to which countries were eligible to launch the euro in January 1999 "will not depend on mathematics .. but the trend."

At the same time, Breuer acknowledged that if countries hit values as high as 3.6 or 3.7 percent of GDP, that would give the euro "a new quality", but fell short of commenting on what the implications of this scenario would be.
He said it would open the door to problems if a discussion were to be raised about watering down EMU goals.
In an earlier address to the conference, Breuer praised Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) as giving impetus for essential market reforms, particularly on European equity markets.
"Europe's fragmented equity markets will develop into the world's third largest equity market thanks to EMU," he said.
"There is no place and no need for 32 stock exchanges and 23 futures and options exchanges. It will be the survival of the fittest."
Breuer also warned against any efforts to undermine the euro project in his speech.
"Instead of worrying about the new developing market ... one must start appreciating the opportunities associated with the euro," he said.
